contract: Append an explicit depth criterion (default DCS2=2), DCS1 DI table in mm and rain threshold in source cm units to scheduled parameters; append deficit_cm and rainfall_cm to requests. DCS1=1 evaluates max(0,deficit+AFGEN(DI)*0.1-rain_reduction), where rain_reduction equals full rainfall only for rainfall>threshold. Reuse existing depth limits, solute bump, rate/duration, split and candidate-event owner in source order. interpolated_depth records the raw DCS1 amount before common limits, or the unchanged DCS2 table value.
guards: DCS1 table follows source DVS [0,2], DI [-100,100] mm and threshold [0,1000]. Bounded supplied deficit in [-1e6,1e6] cm and rainfall in [0,1e6] cm, finite, are candidate availability bounds preventing arithmetic overflow, not new reference physics. Reject unrepresentable AFGEN slope before division. DCS1 request inputs are evaluated only after a timing trigger; active continuation uses stored selected rate. DCS2 default ignores DCS1 fields.
ownership: Existing irrigation_state_t remains the sole candidate event state. No new committed owner, restart format, parser, soil flux publication or scheduler invocation. No changes to Full Richards, mass tolerances or canonical scope.
gates: 100000 source-order comparisons through selected rate/duration and surface or single-node SSDI; independent existing DCS1 helper as second oracle; strict rain and solute boundaries, floor/limits, split/retry and copied-state continuation, no-trigger and active-event input irrelevance, invalid input and default preservation; existing DCS1 oracle, DCS2 bundle and frozen F-APP07 110-interval preservation at O0/O2.
non_goals: Derive crop deficit, invoke calendar, integrate DCS1 into public production driver, book accepted water/solute mass, disk restart or canonical admission.
